sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This past May, the city of Los Angeles rolled out a brand new state-of-the-art feature for bus shelters.
sentences.zh: 今年五月，洛杉矶市为公交候车亭推出了一项全新的尖端设施。

sentences.en: It's called La Sombrita.
sentences.zh: 它叫“La Sombrita”。

sentences.en: La Sombrita is a metal screen that's intended to provide shade for the thousands of people who ride the bus every day.
sentences.zh: La Sombrita 是一块金属屏风，旨在为每天乘坐公交车的成千上万名乘客提供遮阳。

sentences.en: The shade screen is about 2 feet wide, 10 feet tall, and it kind of looks like a curved teal metal surfboard filled with tiny little holes.
sentences.zh: 这块遮阳屏宽约2英尺，高约10英尺，看起来像是一块布满小孔的青色弧形金属冲浪板。

sentences.en: Right away, Angelenos were not happy.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶人立刻就不乐意了。

sentences.en: I was wondering why I was here because I was like, well, what's the point?
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想我为什么会在这儿，因为我觉得，这到底有什么意义？

sentences.en: Criticism has been swift online with people comparing this to a cheese grater.
sentences.zh: 网上的批评声接踵而至，人们把它比作一个奶酪擦丝器。

sentences.en: Many of the online complaints cited La Sombrita's size.
sentences.zh: 许多网络投诉都提到了 La Sombrita 的尺寸问题。

sentences.en: While the designers say La Sombrita can provide shade for two or three people, critics say it doesn't look big enough for even a single person.
sentences.zh: 虽然设计师称 La Sombrita 可以为两到三个人遮阳，但批评者认为它看起来连一个人都遮不住。

sentences.en: And many people are furious about the coSt.
sentences.zh: 而且很多人对它的成本感到愤怒。

sentences.en: The La Sombrita prototype cost around $10,000.
sentences.zh: La Sombrita 原型机的造价约为一万美元。

sentences.en: Clearly, La Sombrita isn't perfect.
sentences.zh: 显然，La Sombrita 并不完美。

sentences.en: But in Los Angeles, a little shade goes a long way.
sentences.zh: 但在洛杉矶，哪怕是一点点阴凉也弥足珍贵。

sentences.en: The controversy around La Sombrita got me thinking about a conversation we had in 2020 with the journalist Sam Block.
sentences.zh: 围绕 La Sombrita 的争议让我想起了我们 2020 年与记者萨姆·布洛克进行的一次谈话。

sentences.en: Sam is working on a book about the politics of shade and how shade coverage in L.A.
sentences.zh: 萨姆正在写一本关于遮阳政治的书，探讨洛杉矶的遮阳覆盖率如何

sentences.en: has become one of the city's biggest hot-button issues.
sentences.zh: 成为了该市最热门的争议话题之一。

sentences.en: Today, we'll get Sam's thoughts about La Sombrita and whether the controversial shade fixture could actually be a good thing for shade-starved Angelenos.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将听听萨姆对 La Sombrita 的看法，以及这个备受争议的遮阳装置是否真的能为渴望阴凉的洛杉矶人带来好处。

sentences.en: But first, my conversation with Sam Block from 2020.
sentences.zh: 但首先，请听我 2020 年与萨姆·布洛克的对话。

sentences.en: What did you notice about Los Angeles when you started walking around the city?
sentences.zh: 当你开始在洛杉矶走动时，你注意到了什么？

sentences.en: What did I notice?
sentences.zh: 我注意到了什么？

sentences.en: I noticed that there was no one around.
sentences.zh: 我注意到周围几乎没有人。

sentences.en: I noticed that the people who were around would have to position themselves in such a way to protect themselves from the sunlight.
sentences.zh: 我注意到那些在外面的人，不得不通过调整位置来躲避阳光。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: I noticed people waiting for the buses behind telephone poles.
sentences.zh: 我注意到人们躲在电线杆后面等公交车。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And I noticed people waiting behind the people, waiting behind telephone poles, because it was only that small sliver of shade that people were protected from the sunlight.
sentences.zh: 我还注意到人们躲在那些躲在电线杆后面的人身后，因为只有那一小片阴影能让人免受阳光直射。

sentences.en: Why is shade so important?
sentences.zh: 为什么遮阳如此重要？

sentences.en: Los Angeles, like most every city in the world, is heating up.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶和世界上几乎所有城市一样，正在变暖。

sentences.en: There are some scientists who I speak to who have found that in hot, dry, arid environments like Los Angeles, but also Phoenix,
sentences.zh: 我采访过一些科学家，他们发现，在像洛杉矶甚至凤凰城这样炎热、干燥、干旱的环境中，

sentences.en: that shade is the most important factor when it comes to human comfort.
sentences.zh: 遮阳是影响人类舒适度的最重要因素。

sentences.en: More than air temperature, more than humidity, more than wind speed.
sentences.zh: 比气温、湿度和风速都更重要。

sentences.en: And there's a close relationship between human thermal comfort and mortality and illness and heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 人类的热舒适度与死亡率、疾病和中暑之间有着密切的联系。

sentences.en: If you don't have shade, if you're not protected from the sun, you can become dizzy, you can become disoriented, you can become confused, lethargic, dehydrated.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有遮阳，如果你没有得到防晒保护，你可能会感到头晕、迷失方向、困惑、昏昏欲睡、脱水。

sentences.en: If you are obese or elderly or pregnant, that can tip into more dangerous things like heart attack or organ failure.
sentences.zh: 如果你肥胖、年长或怀孕，这可能会引发更危险的情况，如心脏病发作或器官衰竭。

sentences.en: And so what is the magnitude of the problem in LA?
sentences.zh: 那么洛杉矶面临的问题有多严重？

sentences.en: There are a few different ways of thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 有几种不同的思考方式。

sentences.en: We can talk about shade in terms of tree canopy, which is a very serious problem.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从树冠覆盖率的角度来谈论遮阳，这是一个非常严重的问题。

sentences.en: Los Angeles has terribly unequal tree canopy.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶的树冠覆盖率极度不平等。

sentences.en: And by tree canopy, I just mean coverage.
sentences.zh: 说到树冠，我指的就是覆盖范围。

sentences.en: Let's say you're in outer space looking down in LA.
sentences.zh: 假设你在太空中俯瞰洛杉矶。

sentences.en: You'll see parts of the city that are covered in green, and you'll see parts of the city that are not, that are baking in asphalt.
sentences.zh: 你会看到城市里有些地方绿意盎然，而有些地方则不然，它们在沥青路面上被炙烤着。

sentences.en: And those, to a T, follow lines of wealth.
sentences.zh: 而这些地方的分布，完全遵循着财富的界线。

sentences.en: It's a problem with tree canopy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个树冠覆盖率的问题。

sentences.en: It's a problem in terms of the built urban form.
sentences.zh: 这也是城市建筑形态的问题。

sentences.en: Los Angeles is notoriously anti-density.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶以反密度著称。

sentences.en: Los Angeles has this image of itself as not being New York City.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶给自己的定位是“非纽约市”。

sentences.en: In fact, being the anti-New York City.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它就是“反纽约市”。

sentences.en: So sunlight and open space is a part of the culture.
sentences.zh: 所以阳光和开放空间是其文化的一部分。

sentences.en: That's not necessarily a problem.
sentences.zh: 这本身不一定是个问题。

sentences.en: But it becomes a problem when you can't escape it.
sentences.zh: 但当你无法逃避它时，这就成了问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there are no tall buildings to provide some measure of shade.
sentences.zh: 所以没有高楼大厦来提供一定程度的遮阳。

sentences.en: I wouldn't go as far as to say there are no tall buildings.
sentences.zh: 我不会说完全没有高楼大厦。

sentences.en: However, there are a few tall buildings.
sentences.zh: 不过，高楼确实很少。

sentences.en: And they're spaced pretty far apart.
sentences.zh: 而且它们分布得相当分散。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're located in certain height districts, downtown being one of them.
sentences.zh: 它们位于特定的高度区，市中心就是其中之一。

sentences.en: And even some areas that city planners have designated to be taller neighborhoods, even today, they're still fought and contested by neighborhood activists.
sentences.zh: 即使是城市规划者指定为高密度社区的一些区域，直到今天，仍然受到社区活动人士的抵制和抗争。

sentences.en: So I've seen little pictures, and I get a sense that Los Angeles used to be greener.
sentences.zh: 我看到过一些老照片，感觉洛杉矶过去绿化更好。

sentences.en: Like, there was a lot of shade.
sentences.zh: 比如，那时候有很多树荫。

sentences.en: So tell me how the city was designed and how it developed into this.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我，这座城市是如何设计并发展成今天这样的？

sentences.en: So time-wise, Los Angeles was a prairie.
sentences.zh: 从时间上讲，洛杉矶曾经是一片草原。

sentences.en: If you look at photos of L.A.
sentences.zh: 如果你看 150 年前的洛杉矶照片，

sentences.en: from 150 years ago, it's all grasslands.
sentences.zh: 到处都是草地。

sentences.en: And when it was settled by the Spanish downtown, which was the original settlement, was laid out according to the law of the Indies.
sentences.zh: 当西班牙人定居时，最初的定居点市中心是按照《印度法律》布局的。

sentences.en: The city would roughly conform to a 45-degree angle.
sentences.zh: 城市大致呈 45 度角布局。

sentences.en: So you could have sunlight in the winter and shade and shadow in the summer.
sentences.zh: 这样你冬天可以晒到太阳，夏天可以享受到阴凉。

sentences.en: So to explain the law of the Indies, what does this mean?
sentences.zh: 那么解释一下《印度法律》，这是什么意思？

sentences.en: The law of the Indies means build your cities at 45 degrees, basically.
sentences.zh: 《印度法律》基本上就是说，把你的城市建成 45 度角。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Completely unlike the way we think of most American cities, which have this sort of north-south, east-west, very rigid grid.
sentences.zh: 这与我们对大多数美国城市的印象完全不同，那些城市通常是南北、东西向的，非常僵化的网格布局。

sentences.en: So you have these original settlements that are laid out in such a way as to be able to create shadow when you need it and also to bestow sunlight also when you need it.
sentences.zh: 所以这些最初的定居点布局方式，既能在需要时创造阴影，也能在需要时引入阳光。

sentences.en: Spanish architecture tends to have a very strong sense of natural comfort.
sentences.zh: 西班牙建筑往往有一种非常强烈的自然舒适感。

sentences.en: So you'll see a lot of these kinds of missions and adobes that have these internal courtyards that are shaded.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到很多这种带有遮阳内庭院的传教所和土坯房。

sentences.en: You'll have covered walkways, paseos.
sentences.zh: 你会有带顶棚的走道，即“paseos”。

sentences.en: And even today, you'll see a lot of this in, like, Spanish revival architecture or, you know, outdoor malls that have goofy Spanish-ish names.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，你也会在西班牙复兴风格的建筑，或者那些有着滑稽西班牙名字的户外购物中心里看到很多这种设计。

sentences.en: Los Angeles was also, in a way, sort of a dusty old west town.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶在某种程度上也曾是一个尘土飞扬的旧西部城镇。

sentences.en: So you think about these covered boardwalks and you think about large canvas awnings that are cooling people who are, you know, living outside and also cooling indoors,
sentences.zh: 所以你会想到那些带顶棚的木板路，想到那些为生活在户外的人们降温，同时也为室内降温的大型帆布遮阳篷，

sentences.en: which at the time didn't have air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 当时室内还没有空调。

sentences.en: And another way that Los Angeles tried to stay cool was through rich, beautiful, kind of flamboyant, not just tree canopy, but a syncretic,
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶试图保持凉爽的另一种方式是，通过丰富、美丽、华丽的，不仅仅是树冠，还有一种融合的、

sentences.en: overwhelming variety of exotic flora and fauna.
sentences.zh: 令人眼花缭乱的各种外来动植物。

sentences.en: So during this period, there was a recognition of the environment and how to be comfortable inside of it.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时期，人们对环境以及如何在其中保持舒适是有认知的。

sentences.en: And when did that go wrong?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候开始出问题的？

sentences.en: Funny that you put it that way.
sentences.zh: 你这么问很有意思。

sentences.en: Things started to go wrong after cheap electricity came down to Los Angeles with the completion of what's now called the Hoover Dam.
sentences.zh: 随着现在被称为胡佛大坝的工程完工，廉价电力进入洛杉矶后，事情就开始变味了。

sentences.en: So you start to see the city rebuild itself and the new development becomes like we see today.
sentences.zh: 于是你开始看到城市重建，新的开发项目变成了我们今天看到的样子。

sentences.en: Hey, you have controlled air conditioning, you have the automobile, which comes to dominate the city in the 30s and the 40s.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你有受控的空调，你有汽车，汽车在 30 和 40 年代开始主宰这座城市。

sentences.en: And with the automobile, you just have a whole new way of seeing the city.
sentences.zh: 有了汽车，你就有了一种看待城市的新方式。

sentences.en: The names of the streets are household words translated into magic.
sentences.zh: 街道的名字变成了家喻户晓的词汇，被赋予了魔力。

sentences.en: Fabulous stacks of freeways, tremendous turnpikes.
sentences.zh: 壮观的高速公路立交桥，宏伟的收费公路。

sentences.en: The city started to think about how to market itself and how to make itself seem more attractive to outsiders.
sentences.zh: 这座城市开始思考如何营销自己，如何让自己对外人更具吸引力。

sentences.en: And this is where you get palm trees.
sentences.zh: 这就是棕榈树出现的原因。

sentences.en: Palm trees, one essayist said, were about as useful for shade as a telephone pole.
sentences.zh: 一位散文家曾说，棕榈树遮阳的作用和电线杆差不多。

sentences.en: She hated them, but the city was enamored of them.
sentences.zh: 她讨厌棕榈树，但这座城市却对它们情有独钟。

sentences.en: And interestingly, you have different philanthropists and celebrities starting to think about trees as being a public good,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，不同的慈善家和名人开始认为树木是一种公共福利，

sentences.en: but the palm tree in particular being one that doesn't just message L.A.
sentences.zh: 但棕榈树尤其被视为一种不仅能传达洛杉矶作为一种半热带天堂的信息，

sentences.en: as a kind of semi-tropical paradise.
sentences.zh: 而且正如玛丽·皮克福德所说，它非常适合坐在车里逛街，因为树干并不粗壮。

sentences.en: But also, as Mary Pickford said, it's very good for window shopping from the seat of your car because the tree trunks aren't that robuSt.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你开车沿着某条大道行驶，你可以看到所有很棒的东西，因为棕榈树非常细。

sentences.en: So if you're driving down some boulevard, you can see all the great stuff because the palm tree is so narrow.
sentences.zh: 所以洛杉矶在 20 世纪 30 年代也被重新规划为单户住宅城市。

sentences.en: So Los Angeles was also rezoned in the 1930s to become a single-family city.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶为了不至于安抚、不至于讨好，而是为了按照联邦住房管理局（FHA）的形象重塑自己，

sentences.en: Los Angeles, in order to sort of not pacify, not suck up, but to sort of remake itself in the image of the FHA,
sentences.zh: 决定所有新建的单户住宅都必须配备前院和侧院。

sentences.en: decided that all new single-family homes had to come with a front and a side yard.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始在它们周围创造出大量的空间。

sentences.en: So you start to create a lot of space around them.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶真的开始讨厌密度的概念了。

sentences.en: Los Angeles really starts to hate the idea of density.
sentences.zh: 那么，当你有这种蔓延的、密度不高的城市时，阴凉是如何分配的？

sentences.en: And so when you have this type of sprawling, not very dense city, how is the shade distributed?
sentences.zh: 分配不均。

sentences.en: Unevenly.
sentences.zh: 阴凉分配给了那些买得起的人。

sentences.en: Shade is distributed to people who can afford it.
sentences.zh: 如果你走进那些被规划为富人住宅区的社区，你会发现人行道非常宽。

sentences.en: If you go into these neighborhoods that were laid out to be wealthy residential enclaves, you have very wide sidewalks.
sentences.zh: 而那条可以种树的草带，被称为“绿化带”，宽度达到了四五英尺，甚至十英尺。

sentences.en: And the strip of grass where you can tree plant, which is called the parkway, becomes four or five, maybe even ten feet wide.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有这些更宽的绿化带时，你就有更大的空间来种植更大、更厚、叶子更茂密的树木。

sentences.en: And when you have these wider parkways, you have a greater space to plant a bigger, thicker, leafier tree.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 所以绿化带就是人行道和马路之间的区域。

sentences.en: So the parkway is the area between the sidewalk and the road.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 这些区域可以很宽，因此可以种树。

sentences.en: And those can be pretty wide and therefore have trees with them.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 在其他被划为红线区域的社区，那些被设计为工人住房、旨在把人们挤在一起的社区，

sentences.en: In other neighborhoods that have been redlined, that were designed as sort of worker housing, that were meant to sort of jam people in together,
sentences.zh: 你没有这种宽阔的住宅人行道。

sentences.en: you don't have these kinds of wide residential sidewalks.
sentences.zh: 相反，你拥有的是非常狭窄的人行道，因为这些社区的设计是为了方便汽车通行。

sentences.en: Instead, what you have are very narrow sidewalks because these neighborhoods are designed to facilitate automobile passage.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有人行道很窄，你真的没有空间去种一棵茂密的树。

sentences.en: So if you have a narrow sidewalk, you don't really have the space to plant a thick, leafy tree.
sentences.zh: 此外，维护绿化带这种半公共空间一直是由业主和租户负责的。

sentences.en: Furthermore, it's been incumbent upon property owners and renters to maintain this sort of semi-public space of the parkway.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为在城市里，人行道上的任何东西，或者产权线以外的任何东西都应该由城市管理。

sentences.en: You would think that in a city, whatever's on the sidewalk, whatever's outside of the property line would be managed by the city.
sentences.zh: 但在洛杉矶历史上并非如此。

sentences.en: That has not historically been the case in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 业主一直有责任将树木浇水至成熟并进行维护。

sentences.en: It's been incumbent upon property owners to water trees to maturity and to maintain them.
sentences.zh: 如果那里有一棵树，那是因为有人主动承担了将其浇水至成熟并照顾它的责任。

sentences.en: If there's a tree there, it's because someone has taken it upon themselves to water it to maturity and to care for it.
sentences.zh: 所以这个过程的每一个环节，人行道相对于街道的设计，富人可以种植和维护树木的事实，

sentences.en: So each part of that process, the design of where the sidewalk is relative to the street, the fact that a person of wealth could plant and maintain a tree,
sentences.zh: 所有这些都导致了遮阳树木分布更加不均匀。

sentences.en: all these things cause more uneven distribution of shade trees.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，在一些社区，比如汉考克公园，那是一个平坦的社区，位于城市中心，被陆地包围。

sentences.en: And I would also add that in some neighborhoods, I'm thinking about a neighborhood called Hancock Park, which is a flat neighborhood, landlocked in the center of the city.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何自然条件使其成为一个郁郁葱葱、绿树成荫的天堂。

sentences.en: There is nothing about it that naturally lends itself over to being a lush, verdant, tree festooned paradise.
sentences.zh: 但该社区被开发为一个排外的富人住宅区。

sentences.en: But the neighborhood was developed as an exclusive wealthy residential enclave.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，电线被埋在了地下。

sentences.en: And when that happened, the power lines were undergrounded.

sentences.en: Because I'm thinking about a park downtown called Pershing Square that up until the 1950s was a tropical paradise.
sentences.zh: 因为我想到市中心有个叫潘兴广场（Pershing Square）的公园，直到20世纪50年代，那里还是个热带天堂。

sentences.en: And after a while, the business elite in the neighborhood decided, first of all, to install underground parking, which gets rid of the whole root system.

sentences.en: So you can no longer plant thicker, denser tree canopy.

sentences.en: And part of the reason why Pershing Square was redeveloped and shorn of its tree canopy is because Los Angeles is a city where residents are worried about crime,
sentences.zh: 潘兴广场之所以被重新开发并砍掉了树冠，部分原因是洛杉矶的居民担心犯罪，

sentences.en: And you can go on Google Street View and go back five, six, seven years, and you can see over time when a pole camera goes up, a mature street tree goes down.
sentences.zh: 你可以在谷歌街景上回看五、六、七年前的影像，你会发现随着时间的推移，当杆式摄像头竖起来时，成熟的行道树就被砍掉了。

sentences.en: So there's just all these selective pressures where other things are just more important.

sentences.en: It just seems like everything is working against it, especially in this city.

sentences.en: And so how do you think about how to balance these, you know, these different factors and their value in an urban setting?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为在城市环境中该如何平衡这些不同的因素及其价值呢？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: There are a few ways to think about this.
sentences.zh: 有几种思考方式。

sentences.en: I mentioned that in Los Angeles, it's homeowners and residents who are responsible for the maintenance and cultivation of street trees.
sentences.zh: 我提到过，在洛杉矶，行道树的维护和培育责任在于房主和居民。

sentences.en: which developer is going to say, let's actually carve out some of our floor space to make an arcade or a portico?
sentences.zh: 哪个开发商会说，我们要腾出一些建筑面积来做一个拱廊或柱廊呢？

sentences.en: So that's a tough sell.
sentences.zh: 所以这很难推销。

sentences.zh: 那么，为什么城市不通过适当的激励措施，鼓励开发商在物业线后创造这种与人行道相连的半公共遮阳环境呢？

sentences.zh: 那单纯种树呢？

sentences.zh: 市政府正在努力种植更多的树。

sentences.en: I am not sufficiently convinced that the city recognizes the infrastructural challenge to planting 90,000 trees because, as we've been talking about,

sentences.en: Or he'll point out these elaborate front yards where you have blue poly tarps just strung across a space or maybe exotic trees that are sort of overflowing into the street.
sentences.zh: 听起来很不错，但我感觉市政府并不总是以同样的方式看待这些事情。

sentences.en: Well, that sounds great to me, but I get the impression that the city doesn't always see things the same way.
sentences.zh: 我发现的是，在私人领域，这些东西是被容忍的。
